fields.text: If your largest single customer or client stopped buying tomorrow, what would happen to the business?

A.text: No single customer accounts for enough of the business for their loss to matter materially

B.text: Losing them would be noticeable, but the business would continue as planned

C.text: Losing them would interrupt revenue and require a deliberate effort to replace it, but the business would recover

D.text: Losing them would materially impair the business for an extended period — plans, capacity or commitments would have to change

E.text: The business could not continue in its current form without restructuring or replacing this relationship

fields.text: If your main route to customers became unavailable — a platform, referral source, intermediary, marketplace, or location — what would happen?

A.text: Customers reach the business through several routes; no single one is essential

B.text: Losing the main route would be noticeable, but the others would carry the business

C.text: Losing it would interrupt new business and require deliberate effort to rebuild reach

D.text: Losing it would materially reduce the flow of new business for an extended period; plans would have to change

E.text: The business has no viable way to reach customers without this route and could not continue in its current form

fields.text: If demand for your single largest product, service, or revenue stream fell away, what would happen?

A.text: Revenue is spread across offerings; no single one is dominant

B.text: The largest offering matters, but its loss would leave a viable business

C.text: Its loss would remove a significant share of revenue, requiring deliberate effort to replace

D.text: Its loss would materially impair the business for an extended period

E.text: The business is substantially this one offering and could not continue in its current form without it

fields.text: If the single market, region, or customer segment you depend on most became inaccessible or unviable, what would happen?

A.text: The business serves several markets or segments; none is essential

B.text: Losing access to the main one would be noticeable but absorbable

C.text: Losing access would interrupt revenue and require deliberate redirection

D.text: Losing access would materially impair the business for an extended period

E.text: The business exists to serve this one market and could not continue in its current form without it

fields.text: If the business could not obtain any additional funding or owner contribution beyond what is already available or committed, what would happen?

A.text: The business funds itself from its own operations and requires no external funding or owner contribution

B.text: It could continue on the funds already available with minor adjustment

C.text: It would have to reduce activity deliberately — slowing spending, deferring plans — but would continue

D.text: It would have to make material cuts to capacity, commitments, or plans to continue

E.text: The business could not continue in its current form on the funds already available or committed

fields.text: If a major expected payment to the business were delayed by a month, what would happen?

A.text: A delay would not affect the business; reserves or cash flow absorb it easily

B.text: It would be absorbed within normal operations

C.text: It would require deliberate action — deferring payments, drawing on facilities, chasing collection — but obligations would be met

D.text: Obligations to staff, suppliers, or lenders would be at risk and commitments would have to change

E.text: The business could not meet its obligations and could not continue in its current form

fields.text: If a major cost the business depends on rose sharply — materials, labour, energy, rent, borrowing, or currency — what would happen?

A.text: Costs are stable or fully passable to customers; a sharp rise would not matter

B.text: It would reduce margin noticeably but be absorbed

C.text: It would require deliberate action — repricing, renegotiation, cost reduction — to protect viability

D.text: It would materially impair profitability for an extended period; plans and capacity would have to change

E.text: The business could not remain viable in its current form at those cost levels

fields.text: If your main lender, landlord, investor, or financing arrangement withdrew or materially changed its terms, what would happen?

A.text: No lender, landlord, or investor relationship is material to the business

B.text: Withdrawal would be absorbed; alternatives are readily available

C.text: Withdrawal would require deliberate effort to replace, with some disruption

D.text: Withdrawal would materially impair the business for an extended period; alternatives are scarce or much costlier

E.text: The business could not continue in its current form without this arrangement

fields.text: If the person most central to the business became unavailable without warning, what would happen?

A.text: No individual holds knowledge, relationships or authority that others could not cover

B.text: Their absence would be inconvenient; others could cover within normal operations

C.text: Their absence would interrupt work and require deliberate reallocation, but the business would function

D.text: Their absence would materially impair the business for an extended period; commitments would have to change

E.text: The business could not continue in its current form without this person

fields.text: If the system, platform, software, or equipment the business most depends on became unavailable, what would happen?

A.text: No single system is essential; alternatives are readily usable

B.text: Loss would be inconvenient; a replacement is in place or immediately available

C.text: Loss would interrupt operations while a replacement was put in place

D.text: Loss would materially impair operations for an extended period; there is no ready replacement

E.text: Operations depend entirely on this system and could not continue in their current form without it

fields.text: If your most important supplier, subcontractor, or external provider stopped supplying, what would happen?

A.text: Inputs are available from several sources; no provider is essential

B.text: Loss would be absorbed by switching to an existing alternative

C.text: Loss would interrupt delivery while an alternative was found and brought up to standard

D.text: Loss would materially impair delivery for an extended period; alternatives are costly, slow, or of lower quality

E.text: No adequate alternative exists and the business could not continue in its current form

fields.text: If the business lost access to its main premises, site, or location, what would happen?

A.text: The business is not tied to any particular location

B.text: Loss of the main site would be absorbed — work could continue elsewhere with minor disruption

C.text: Loss would interrupt operations while alternative space was arranged

D.text: Loss would materially impair operations for an extended period; suitable alternatives are scarce or costly

E.text: The business is inseparable from this location and could not continue in its current form elsewhere

fields.text: If any current legal dispute, claim, or regulatory finding against the business resolved unfavourably, what would happen?

A.text: No dispute, claim, or regulatory finding exists

B.text: One exists; an unfavourable outcome would be absorbed

C.text: An unfavourable outcome would require a deliberate financial or operational response

D.text: An unfavourable outcome would materially impair the business for an extended period

E.text: An unfavourable outcome would leave the business unable to continue in its current form

fields.text: If a licence, permit, registration, or approval the business needs were withdrawn or not renewed, what would happen?

A.text: The business requires no licence, permit, or approval to operate

B.text: Loss would restrict some activity, but the business would continue

C.text: Loss would suspend part of the business until it was restored or replaced

D.text: Loss would materially impair the business for an extended period

E.text: The business cannot legally operate without it and could not continue in its current form

fields.text: If the rules, subsidies, tariffs, or policies your business relies on changed materially, what would happen?

A.text: The business does not depend on any particular rule, subsidy, tariff, or policy

B.text: A material change would be absorbed

C.text: A material change would require deliberate adjustment to pricing, sourcing, or operations

D.text: A material change would materially impair the business for an extended period

E.text: The business's viability rests on the current rules and could not continue in its current form without them

fields.text: If ownership of a key asset, brand, or intellectual property the business relies on were challenged, or found to sit outside the business, what would happen?

A.text: Ownership of everything the business relies on is clear and held by the business

B.text: A challenge would be resolvable without material effect

C.text: A challenge would require a deliberate legal or commercial response

D.text: A successful challenge would materially impair the business for an extended period

E.text: A successful challenge would remove something the business could not continue in its current form without

fields.text: If the current direction of demand in your market continued for another two years, what would it mean for the business?

A.text: Demand in the market is growing; continuation is favourable

B.text: Demand is broadly stable; continuation would require no change

C.text: Demand is softening; continuation would require a deliberate response to hold position

D.text: Demand is declining enough that continuation would force material changes to plans, capacity, or commitments

E.text: Continuation would leave the business unable to continue in its current form

fields.text: If a well-resourced competitor targeted your main customers directly, what would happen?

A.text: Customers would not realistically move; the position is protected

B.text: Some pressure on price or volume, absorbed within normal operations

C.text: The business would need a deliberate response to hold its customers

D.text: It would lose enough business to force material changes to plans or capacity

E.text: It could not hold enough of its customer base to continue in its current form

fields.text: If a known unresolved problem in what you deliver affected customers at scale, what would happen?

A.text: No known unresolved problem exists in what the business delivers

B.text: One exists; at scale it would cause complaints handled within normal operations

C.text: At scale it would require deliberate remediation and customer recovery effort

D.text: At scale it would materially damage customer relationships or reputation for an extended period

E.text: At scale it would leave the business unable to continue in its current form

fields.text: If a materially better or cheaper alternative to what you offer became widely available, what would happen?

A.text: What the business offers is not readily substitutable

B.text: Some customers would switch; the business would continue as planned

C.text: The business would need to respond deliberately — price, features, positioning — to retain customers

D.text: It would lose enough business to force material changes to plans or capacity

E.text: The offering would be displaced and the business could not continue in its current form
